steps.title: Our stock in three hospitals

steps.purpose: Read Corvale General's approved interchanges for these items.

steps.purpose: Run the semantic layer's key rules (NDC and unit of use) over each hospital's stock, and name the rows they reject.
steps.finding: 11 stock rows across the system fail the NDC rule; 0 of them are this drug. Every row is in a shared unit of use.

explanation.headline: FDA's records trace our supply to a plant classified OAI 809 days before the posting

sentences.text: FDA first posted the sterile water injection shortage on 2021-11-23 and it remains current as of 2026-10-21.
An FDA inspection at Pfizer Healthcare India Private Limited (FEI 3008316085) ended 2019-09-06 and was classified OAI, 809 days before the shortage posting.
A Warning Letter was issued to the same plant on 2020-03-25, 608 days before the posting.
Nephron SC, LLC (FEI 3010892830) received a Warning Letter on 2020-09-22, 427 days before the posting, and later an OAI inspection ending 2022-04-20, 148 days after the posting.
Hospira, Inc. (FEI 1021343) had a VAI inspection ending 2019-11-21, 733 days before the posting.
The rule-based best option is to buy from American Regent, Inc., which is not on FDA's shortage list today and whose plant last received a VAI inspection on 2024-04-24.

memory.text: Decision on lidocaine: switch lidocaine 1% 30 mL vials to 5 mL vials in the ED to reduce waste during the shortage. Rationale: Single-dose waste was a third of use (demo history). Approved by Alex Morgan, PharmD.

Decision on acetaminophen, in the approver's words: "Transfer 22 bags of 10 mg/mL, 100 mL from Corvale East to Corvale Lakeside". Rationale: Acetaminophen is not on FDA's shortage list as of 2026-10-21; internal inventory shows Corvale Lakeside at 8.8 days on hand.. Approved by Jordan Hale, PharmD.

Decision on cisplatin: transfer cisplatin between Corvale hospitals weekly instead of buying grey-market stock. Rationale: Grey-market offers were 6 to 10 times contract price with unverifiable pedigree (demo history). Approved by Jordan Hale, PharmD.
